# Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living — concept pack (small)

## How it works

- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation advises avoiding driving when fatigued, when medication is wearing off, or when starting a new medicine. (low confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/activities-daily-living/driving

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Travel guidance recommends carrying extra medication and keeping medication in carry-on luggage rather than depending on checked bags. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/traveling · keywords: Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living · also: https://davisphinneyfoundation.org/blog/travel-with-greater-ease-parkinsons/
- [statement] In a 2014 randomized trial of 191 people with PD and daily-activity difficulties, a 10-week home occupational-therapy intervention improved self-perceived daily activity performance at 3 months compared with usual care without occupational therapy; the endpoint does not establish disease modification. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24726066/
- [statement] In a Parkinson’s UK forum discussion, one traveler with PD reported that advance wheelchair assistance helped with airport queues and walking; this is an individual experience rather than evidence that one itinerary is best for everyone. (low confidence) — https://forum.parkinsons.org.uk/t/long-distance-air-travel-uk-to-australia-advice-please/43760

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A PD diagnosis alone does not determine whether someone can drive safely; the Parkinson’s Foundation advises assessment of the individual’s symptoms and other age-related changes. (low confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/activities-daily-living/driving
- [statement] Driving fitness assessment should consider motor function, cognition, vision, sleepiness and medication effects; specialist on-road and off-road assessment can help resolve concerns. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10928339/ · keywords: Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living · also: https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/activities-daily-living/driving
- [statement] For time-zone travel, the Parkinson’s Foundation advises preserving the prescribed intervals between doses; Davis Phinney Foundation travel guidance likewise recommends planning a consistent medication schedule. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/traveling · keywords: Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living · also: https://davisphinneyfoundation.org/blog/travel-with-greater-ease-parkinsons/
- [statement] Travel planning guidance recommends allowing extra time, scheduling rest around arrival, and avoiding an overloaded itinerary. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/traveling · keywords: Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living · also: https://davisphinneyfoundation.org/blog/travel-with-greater-ease-parkinsons/
- [statement] How long a person continues working after PD diagnosis varies with job demands, symptoms and circumstances; Parkinson’s Europe describes contrasting personal experiences of continuing work and leaving work. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/employment · keywords: Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living · also: https://parkinsonseurope.org/parkinsonslife/navigating-the-workplace-with-parkinsons-disease/
- [statement] Suggested workplace adaptations include scheduling difficult tasks during better-functioning periods, breaks, ergonomic or computer adaptations, and exploring flexible hours or telecommuting where feasible. (low confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/employment
- [statement] Occupational therapy can tailor routines and task strategies to a person’s priorities, including dressing, cooking, handwriting, work and driving; the plan is tested and adjusted to the person’s needs. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/occupational-therapy · keywords: Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living · also: https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/physical-occupational-speech-therapies
- [statement] A 2018 driving meta-analysis found poorer on-road and simulator outcomes in PD, but no significant difference in self-reported real-life crash involvement; its authors cautioned against PD-specific relicensure mandates based on self-reported crash data alone. (low confidence) — https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000006132
